sources.name: SWE-bench
sources.claim: SWE-bench tasks give an AI system an issue text and repository, then evaluate the generated patch with fail-to-pass tests.
sources.use_in_this_repo: A Story eval tasks should be issue-like and patch-based, with explicit fail-to-pass gates for the broken behavior.

sources.name: SWE-bench Verified
sources.claim: Verified is a human-validated subset intended to improve reliability of coding-agent evaluation.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Task quality needs human review: clear prompt, fair checker, realistic issue, and no ambiguous hidden expectation.

sources.name: OpenAI SWE-bench Verified launch
sources.claim: Human validation can filter unclear or low-quality tasks from a larger SWE benchmark.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Every A Story task should have a review checklist before it becomes part of the stable suite.

sources.name: OpenAI on SWE-bench Verified limitations
sources.claim: Overly specific tests, underspecified task statements, and environment sensitivity can underreport capable agents.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Hidden checkers must validate contract behavior without rejecting legitimate alternate fixes; prompts must be explicit enough to avoid one-right-patch traps.

sources.name: OpenAI coding-eval data quality audit
sources.claim: OpenAI's 2026 coding-eval audit identifies misleading prompts, overly strict tests, underspecified prompts, and low-coverage tests as distinct benchmark failure classes.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Every task review must compare prompt requirements with checker coverage, reject hidden implementation requirements, and prove the checker cannot pass an incomplete or no-op solution.

sources.name: SWE-bench-Live
sources.claim: Continuously updated benchmarks reduce contamination and better reflect live software development.
sources.use_in_this_repo: The suite should evolve from fresh creator corrections, wiki-health findings, closeout blocks, and carousel failures.

sources.name: OpenAI evaluation best practices
sources.claim: OpenAI's current eval guidance emphasizes repeatable tasks, clear graders, and measuring behavior rather than relying on vibes.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Keep A Story evals fixture-backed, grader-backed, and separated between mechanical contract checks and creative rubric judgment.

sources.name: OpenAI Evals guide
sources.claim: OpenAI's eval documentation centers datasets, graders, runs, and reports as the core loop for evaluating AI behavior.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Map those ideas to the local harness: task fixtures are datasets, deterministic checkers are graders, runner output is the report, and repeated runs protect against instruction drift.

sources.name: UTBoost SWE-bench analysis
sources.claim: Coding-agent patch evaluation commonly combines fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Each task deep spec must state both the failing behavior that should flip and the regression surface that should remain stable.

sources.name: GenEval
sources.claim: Holistic image metrics can miss fine-grained compositional failures; object detection can evaluate co-occurrence, count, position, and attributes at instance level.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Visual QA must compare expected and observed people/entities per slide instead of allowing overall style or prompt alignment to average away a duplicate character.

sources.name: VIEScore
sources.claim: Explainable conditional-image evaluation separates semantic consistency, perceptual quality, and overall score while returning rationale.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Keep semantic scene compliance separate from aesthetic quality and preserve concrete failure reasons in structured visual QA.

sources.name: GEdit-Bench evaluation
sources.claim: Instruction-guided image editing is evaluated across semantic consistency and perceptual quality, and VLM judge scores have measurable run-to-run volatility.
sources.use_in_this_repo: Pair any VLM review with deterministic structured invariants such as exact people counts, unexpected-entity lists, text, brandmark, and dimensions.

sources.name: NVIDIA agent skills catalog
sources.claim: Published skills are paired with task-specific evaluation datasets and benchmark reports rather than relying on instructions alone.
sources.use_in_this_repo: The carousel skill change ships with ASTO-019, a materialized failure fixture, a deterministic checker, pass-to-pass coverage, and focused tests.
